hero.tagline: The World's Stage Comes to the World's City
hero.description: New York — home to MetLife Stadium — will host the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final. There's no bigger stage on Earth, and NYC delivers an unmatched atmosphere for the beautiful game.

stadium.name: MetLife Stadium
stadium.address: 1 MetLife Stadium Dr, East Rutherford, NJ 07073
stadium.transport: Take the NJ Transit train from Penn Station to Meadowlands Station — about 30 minutes. Game-day shuttle buses also operate from the Port Authority Bus Terminal.

transport.summary: NYC has the best public transit in North America. The subway runs 24/7 and connects to NJ Transit for MetLife.
tips: Get an OMNY card for contactless subway/bus payments
NJ Transit game-day trains run from Penn Station — buy tickets in advance
Avoid Uber/Lyft near the stadium on match days — surge pricing is brutal
Allow 90 minutes from Midtown Manhattan to your seat

fan_zones.name: NYC Fan Hub — Central Park
fan_zones.description: A major fan gathering area expected near Central Park during the tournament, with giant screens, food vendors, and live entertainment. Free entry. Check local listings for confirmed details.

fan_zones.name: Times Square Big Screen
fan_zones.description: Times Square screens broadcast all World Cup matches. Massive street party atmosphere on game days.

quick_facts.matches_hosted: 8 matches — Group stage and the Final (July 19)
quick_facts.fan_hub_status: Major fan events expected across New York and New Jersey

weather.june: Warm and humid, with highs often in the upper 70s to mid 80s Fahrenheit.
weather.july: Hotter and humid, with afternoon storms possible and warm nights across the metro area.
packing_tips: Pack comfortable walking shoes for subway, train, and city walking days
Bring a light rain shell for summer storms
Use breathable clothing and plan shade or indoor breaks on long sightseeing days

airports.name: Newark Liberty International Airport
airports.distance_to_stadium: Closest major airport to MetLife Stadium
transfer_options: Best airport for Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark, and Meadowlands hotel stays
Taxi/rideshare is the simplest route to many New Jersey hotels
Rail links connect into New York Penn Station for Manhattan stays
airports.notes: Usually the most convenient airport for match-first travelers focused on the stadium.

airports.name: LaGuardia Airport
airports.distance_to_stadium: Convenient for many domestic flights but across the river from the stadium
transfer_options: Best for Queens, Midtown East, and some Manhattan itineraries
Expect bridge/tunnel traffic when crossing toward New Jersey
airports.notes: Good domestic option, less direct for match-day stadium logistics.

airports.name: John F. Kennedy International Airport
airports.distance_to_stadium: Farthest of the three major airports from MetLife Stadium
transfer_options: AirTrain and rail connections can reach Manhattan, but stadium access still requires New Jersey transit planning
airports.notes: Best for international fares and flight choice, not for shortest stadium transfer.

public_transit: Use NJ Transit service to Meadowlands Station when event trains are operating
Most Manhattan-based fans should plan around New York Penn Station and NJ Transit
Buy rail tickets early and expect crowded post-match platforms
rideshare: Rideshare can work before matches but becomes slow and expensive after full-time
If using rideshare after the match, walk to a designated pickup area and expect delays
driving_parking: Expect heavy traffic around the Meadowlands before and after matches
Driving is easier for New Jersey hotel stays than Manhattan hotel stays
walking_biking: MetLife is not walkable from Manhattan
Jersey City and Hoboken are walkable neighborhoods for hotel stays, but still require transit or car service to the stadium
match_day_tips: Leave at least 90 minutes from Midtown Manhattan to your seat
Stay near Penn Station, Hoboken, Jersey City, or Meadowlands if stadium access is the top priority
Keep your return route flexible because post-match transit will be crowded

fan_hubs.name: Manhattan Fan Hub
fan_hubs.description: Large public viewing and sponsor-style fan activity is expected in central New York areas. Treat exact locations and schedules as pending until local organizers publish details.
transport_tips: Best for fans staying in Manhattan, Queens, Brooklyn, or Jersey City
Use subway and walking rather than driving into Manhattan

fan_hubs.name: New Jersey Match-Day Base
fan_hubs.location: Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark, and Meadowlands
fan_hubs.description: New Jersey is the practical stadium side of the market. Fans prioritizing match-day logistics should consider staying or gathering west of the Hudson.

neighborhoods.name: Midtown Manhattan
neighborhoods.best_for: first-time visitors, Penn Station access, classic sightseeing
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Excellent subway and rail access; busy but convenient
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Best Manhattan base for NJ Transit via Penn Station
neighborhoods.description: The simplest New York base if you want iconic city energy and a direct path toward stadium trains.

neighborhoods.name: Chelsea / Flatiron
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Strong subway access and easy rides to Penn Station
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Short subway/taxi ride to Penn Station before NJ Transit
neighborhoods.description: A polished Manhattan option with better food and nightlife access than staying only around Times Square.

neighborhoods.name: Jersey City
neighborhoods.best_for: skyline views, New Jersey access, slightly calmer hotel base
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: PATH access to Manhattan; choose hotels near waterfront or PATH stations
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Often easier by car/rideshare than Manhattan, depending on event traffic
neighborhoods.description: A smart compromise for fans who want New York views and New Jersey-side stadium logistics.

neighborhoods.name: Hoboken
neighborhoods.best_for: bars, walkable nightlife, younger fan groups
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Very walkable with PATH and ferry options
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Better than most Manhattan neighborhoods for New Jersey-side travel
neighborhoods.description: A strong fan base for bars and group trips, especially if you want nightlife without staying in Manhattan.

neighborhoods.name: Meadowlands / Secaucus
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Less walkable and less scenic, but practical for the stadium
neighborhoods.description: Choose this if the match is the main event and you care less about classic New York sightseeing.

booking_links.label: Compare New York / New Jersey hotels on Booking.com

supporter_groups: Supporter culture spans both New York City and New Jersey, with strong bar scenes around Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Hoboken, and Jersey City
soccer_culture.community_notes: The market is really New York / New Jersey, not just New York City. International fan communities, club bars, and immigrant neighborhoods make it one of the strongest soccer regions in North America.

tourist_hits.name: Central Park
tourist_hits.notes: Best low-cost reset between matches, especially for groups staying in Manhattan.

tourist_hits.name: Times Square
tourist_hits.notes: Chaotic, crowded, and iconic; good for first-time visitors but not where everyone should stay.

tourist_hits.name: Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island
tourist_hits.notes: Book timed tickets early if visiting around peak tournament dates.

local_favorites.name: Hoboken waterfront
local_favorites.notes: Skyline views, bars, and easier New Jersey-side logistics.

local_favorites.name: Queens food neighborhoods
local_favorites.notes: Excellent for international food and fan communities.

local_favorites.name: Brooklyn soccer bars
local_favorites.notes: Better local atmosphere than many Midtown tourist bars.

recommendations.name: Koreatown and Midtown sports bars
recommendations.notes: Convenient before or after Penn Station stadium travel.

recommendations.name: Hoboken bar crawl
recommendations.notes: Good New Jersey-side option for groups after non-stadium watch parties.

local_resources.emergency_info: Use 911 for emergencies. Check MTA and NJ Transit alerts before stadium travel.

walk_bike.walkability_summary: Manhattan, Hoboken, Jersey City waterfront, Brooklyn, and Queens neighborhoods are highly walkable, but stadium travel still requires rail, bus, or car service.
walk_bike.bikeability_summary: Citi Bike is useful for short city trips, not for getting to MetLife Stadium.
walk_bike.bike_share_notes: Use Citi Bike for short neighborhood hops and waterfront rides; avoid relying on bikes for match-day stadium logistics.

pickup_soccer.name: Pier 40
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Popular soccer facility with leagues and pickup-style activity; check permits and schedules.

pickup_soccer.name: McCarren Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Good casual soccer and park atmosphere for fans staying in Brooklyn.

pickup_soccer.name: Liberty State Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Open park space with skyline views; better for casual kicking around than formal pickup.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Hudson River Greenway
outdoors_day_trips.notes: One of the best low-stress outdoor routes for visitors.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Liberty State Park
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Great skyline and harbor views from the New Jersey side.

outdoors_day_trips.name: The High Line
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Best early or late to avoid peak crowds.

safety_tips: Plan stadium travel around NJ Transit and event-specific service, not just normal map estimates
Avoid assuming MetLife Stadium is in New York City; it is in East Rutherford, New Jersey
Keep bags light and check stadium bag rules before leaving your hotel
Expect very crowded trains and platforms after marquee matches
